oewn-01619805-v.learner: to put or fix something firmly in or on a base.
examples: She seated the camera firmly on the tripod before taking the picture.

oewn-02338975-v.learner: to put seats into a place.
examples: The builders seated the new hall with rows of wooden benches.

oewn-02389417-v.learner: to put someone into an office or position in a ceremony or in a formal way.
examples: The new bishop was seated in the cathedral last Sunday.

oewn-02339298-v.learner: to fit a seat onto a chair.
examples: He seated the old chair with woven cane.

oewn-00086649-n.learner: the taking and keeping of someone's property until they pay a debt or settle a claim.
examples: The landlord used distress to take the tenant's furniture until the rent was paid.

oewn-01038191-v.learner: to put someone or something in a dangerous, unfavourable, or difficult position.
examples: The captain's poor decision exposed the whole crew.

oewn-02142175-v.learner: to let something be seen, as if by taking a cover off it.
examples: Pulling back the rug exposed an old trapdoor in the floor.

oewn-01342187-v.learner: to take off all or some of your clothes so that your body can be seen.
examples: The man was arrested for exposing himself in the park.

connotation.why: implies an indecent display, not plain undressing

oewn-00854877-v.learner: to show that something is false while making fun of it, especially claims or ideas that pretend to be more than they are.
examples: The article exposed the healer's grand claims and made him a laughing stock.

connotation.why: casts the target as false or pretentious

oewn-02117913-v.learner: to let light fall on photographic film.
examples: She exposed the film for two seconds.

oewn-00616135-v.learner: to abandon someone or something by leaving them outside in the open air.
examples: In the old story, the baby was exposed on a hillside and left to die.

oewn-01106429-v.learner: to get the better of someone, usually not because they did anything wrong or were weak.
examples: The small army fought bravely but was overcome by far greater numbers.

oewn-01065210-v.learner: to decide what is to happen if certain things occur, especially by adding a condition or rule.
examples: The will provides that the house goes to the eldest son if the widow dies.

oewn-02224224-v.learner: to supply what is needed to live, or to earn a living.
examples: After the accident she was the only one in the family who could provide.

oewn-02727313-v.learner: to make something possible or give a chance for it, or to let something be reached or let it remain.
examples: The wide hall provides room for more chairs if they are needed.

oewn-02381380-v.learner: to mount or put up something, such as a defence.
examples: The town provided a stout defence against the attack.

oewn-01211710-n.learner: help given at a time of trouble.
examples: The charity sent relief to the families who lost their homes in the flood.
The workers were given an hour's relief at noon.

oewn-07371701-n.learner: a change that makes things better.
examples: After a week of storms there was some relief in the weather.

oewn-01090092-n.learner: help given to people who are old, poor, or disabled.
examples: After losing his job, he had to go on relief.

oewn-10667676-n.learner: a person who takes over from another, for example when things become dangerous or hard.
examples: The guard waited for his relief to arrive at midnight.

oewn-13312014-n.learner: in law, what a court gives to put right a wrong done to someone.
examples: The company asked the court for relief from the unfair contract.

oewn-04080781-n.learner: a kind of sculpture in which shapes are carved on a surface so that they stand out from the background.
examples: The temple walls were covered with reliefs of dancing figures.

oewn-01077491-n.learner: the act of freeing a city or town that an enemy has surrounded and cut off.
examples: The general marched north with fresh troops for the relief of the city.

oewn-12950543-n.learner: a tropical bush or small tree that stays green all year, grown widely in places such as China, Japan and India, and from which tea leaves come.
examples: Tea grows well on the cool, wet hillsides of northern India.

oewn-00298575-r.learner: in a short, sudden, and rude way.
examples: "I'm busy," she said shortly, and shut the door.

connotation.why: casts the speaker's brevity as rude

examples: Her skirt ended shortly below the knee.

oewn-04314757-n.learner: a thin strip of metal or bone used to make a piece of clothing, such as a corset, stiff.
examples: One of the stays in her corset had snapped.

oewn-04314557-n.learner: on a ship, a heavy rope or wire cable that holds up a mast or other pole.
examples: The wind howled through the stays as the ship rolled.

oewn-04352106-n.learner: a room used for reading, writing, and studying.
examples: After dinner he went to his study to write letters.
Botany is the study of plants.

oewn-05792247-n.learner: careful thought and reflection about something.
examples: May I ask whether these pleasing attentions proceed from the impulse of the moment, or are the result of previous study?

oewn-05713302-n.learner: a state of being lost deep in thought.
examples: She sat by the window in a deep study and did not hear him come in.

oewn-07233130-n.learner: a written report that describes what a person or group has found out.
examples: A new study shows that children sleep less than they used to.

oewn-07062685-n.learner: a piece written to help a performer improve one part of their skill.
examples: The pianist practised a study for the left hand.

oewn-10685903-n.learner: a person who learns things by heart quickly and easily, such as the lines for a part in a play.
examples: He is a quick study and knew all his lines by the second day.
